new_entities.name: Muscular strength
new_entities.description: Maximal force production during resistance exercise tasks.

edges.effect_quant: Across pooled resistance-training studies, HMB generally does not add meaningful strength gains beyond training or placebo.
edges.population: adults using resistance training or athletic conditioning
edges.mechanism: If HMB meaningfully improved recovery or reduced muscle protein breakdown during training, extra strength gains might follow over time. The pooled trial evidence has not shown that pattern consistently, suggesting the theoretical recovery benefit is too small or too context-dependent to matter for most training populations.
edges.summary: The current evidence does not support HMB as a reliable strength enhancer. Across meta-analyses in older adults, young resistance-trained subjects, and competitive athletes, pooled strength outcomes stay close to null, making this a good example of a supplement with stronger marketing than data.
edges.caveats: The neutral conclusion here applies to routine training settings, not necessarily to hospital, cachectic, or highly catabolic contexts. Short interventions and heterogeneous training protocols may also obscure very small benefits, but nothing in the current pooled literature suggests a robust effect.

evidence.citation: Wang G et al 2026 Age Ageing
evidence.notes: Efficacy of HMB supplementation as an adjunct to resistance training in older adults: a comprehensive meta-analysis.
